title: autoplaybook: inference cost onramp + quant compatibility scanner
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers onboarding to Redwood often overprovision inference defaults (large batch shapes, aggressive KV retention, and overly conservative quantization) which increases unit cost and slows time-to-value for Dedicated/Private installs. This PR introduces an "autoplaybook" CLI and library that (1) generates a curated defaults catalog (batching + cache + quant profiles) tailored to a tenant's sampled workload, (2) provides an automated quant-compatibility scanner that statically checks model artifacts and runtime kernels for risky quant fallbacks, and (3) exposes a dry-run/eval mode to simulate unit economics before applying defaults. Summary of changes: Added CLI scaffold (cmd/autoplaybook) that accepts workload traces, a tenant manifest, and returns a recommended profile bundle; implemented a lightweight defaults catalog schema and validator (pkg/econ/catalog), a quant compatibility scanner that runs against model artifacts and kernel/memory heuristics (pkg/quant/compat), integrated simulation hooks for unit-econ dry-runs (pkg/sim) and telemetry events to Redwood Console (telemetry/econ/events). The description below lists the checkboxes and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] CLI scaffolding and help text - [x] defaults catalog schema + YAML examples - [x] quant compatibility scanner with kernel heuristics and diagnostic hints - [x] dry-run simulation (cost projection) + telemetry emission - [x] unit/integration tests for catalog <> scanner interactions - [x] docs/console integration guide - [x] feature-flag gated rollout for Dedicated and Private Reasoning and constraints: The scanner is conservative by default: it flags unsafe quant paths but will not automatically mutate model artifacts. The autoplaybook generates recommended profiles but does not apply them without an explicit tenant approval step. We intentionally leave operator approval in the flow to avoid silent regressions. Backwards compatibility: CLI and library are additive. Existing APIs not modified. Performance: simulation runs are inexpensive (single-process trace replay) and scale linearly with sample size; the scanner uses cached kernel metadata to avoid repeated binary introspection. Release notes: Introduce autoplaybook CLI to generate tenant defaults and a quant-compatibility scanner to validate model serving readiness. No breaking changes. Migration: Operators can run "autoplaybook --dry-run" against a tenant sample and review recommended profile bundle in Console prior to applying. Security: scanner reads model artifacts and kernel metadata; access controlled by existing artifact read permissions. Monitoring: emits telemetry/econ.recommendation and telemetry/econ.scan.warning events (see telemetry/econ/events) for Console dashboards. Rollout plan: gated behind feature-flag "econ.autoplaybook". Stage 1: internal dogfood (1 week) with infra team. Stage 2: opt-in beta for selected customers (2 weeks). Stage 3: GA after customer feedback and additional perf tuning. Related work: ENG-4123 (tenant defaults generator), ENG-4180 (quant scanner heuristics), SUP-728 (customer cost support ticket).

review_thread: Diego Ramos: Nice direction. Can you add an extra unit test that covers a mixed batch/stream workload? The sim currently assumes all requests are small chat-style which skews recommendations.
Asha Patel (author): Good catch. Added tests to tests/econ/catalog_test.go and extended sim to accept a 'mix' sampling mode. See second commit.
Lin Park: Scanner looks solid but we need clearer remediation guidance in the Console UI for flagged kernels. Add an RFC link or docs pointer.
Asha Patel: Added docs/autoplaybook.md with a remediation section and a short RFC link to ENG-4180. Also added CI note reminding reviewers to check kernel-version compatibility matrix.
Maya Singh: CI integration job failed on first run due to flaky e2e sim. Reran and it passed. Please squash the two sim fixes into one commit during the final merge.
Asha Patel: Squashed commits and cleaned up logs. Ready for merge.
Diego Ramos: Approved after seeing the added mixed workload test + simulated cost graphs in telemetry
ci_checks: integration-tests: initial run failed (flaky sim) -> re-run -> pass
bench/perf: pass (cost projection runs in ~120ms for 1k-sample) - note: avg latency regression 2% in worst-case synthetic scenario; acceptable for opt-in beta
release_notes: Add autoplaybook CLI and library to generate tenant-specific batching/caching/quant defaults and a quant compatibility scanner. Operators can dry-run cost simulations before applying recommendations. Feature-flag gated. No breaking changes.
notes_for_operators: Run: ./autoplaybook --tenant <tenant-id> --sample traces.json --dry-run to receive a recommended defaults bundle. Review events in Console under "econ.recommendation". To apply: follow operator guide in docs/autoplaybook.md. Feature flag: econ.autoplaybook must be enabled.
qa_approach: Unit tests for catalog validation and scanner heuristics, integration tests that replay sampled workload traces, and a small internal dogfood rollout. Performance benchmark included in CI (scripts/ci/autoplaybook_integration.sh).
post_merge_actions: Flip feature flag to beta for internal dogfood, create a short runbook for SRE to monitor telemetry/econ.scan.warning events, schedule a 2-week beta cohort, and open a follow-up PR to tighten quant heuristics based on beta feedback (ENG-4180 follow-up).
